chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When Adam (peace be upon him) was sent down from Paradise to Al-Safa, and Hawwa (peace be upon him) to Al-Marwa, and she had been combing her hair in Paradise with perfume from the perfumes of Paradise. So when she came to be on earth, she said: 'What hope is there for me in combing, while I am loathsome to my hair?' So she loosened her braids, and from her combing which she used to comb with in Paradise, there scattered [particles], and the wind carried it and cast most of it in India. Thus, it is due to that, came to be the perfume in India.
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah, from Ali ibn Hassan – similar to it.

He said: 'And in another Hadith: She loosened her braids, so Allah sent upon what was therein from that perfume, a wind, so it descended in the East and the West. Thus, the origination of the perfume is from that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the origin of perfume according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* links the physical origin of perfume to the Fall of Hawwa, interpreting the scattering of her hair's perfume as a divine distribution of blessings across the earth, particularly to India. It reflects the Shia tradition of connecting earthly phenomena to primordial events in Paradise, offering a spiritual dimension to material goods. The hadith also includes a variant where the wind distributes the scent globally, emphasizing the universal nature of this divine gift.
